summary.name: Things I Learned Managing Site Reliability for Some of the World's Busiest Gambling Sites
summary.one_liner: A first-person essay by a former third-line SRE lead at a gambling backend company, on the process, documentation, triage, and culture practices that made an incident-response operation work.
use_cases: Setting up incident runbooks for an operations team
Deciding how to structure triage and escalation
Choosing or migrating a ticketing system for ops
Onboarding junior engineers into an SRE function
summary.what_it_does: The page is a long blog essay rather than a software tool. The author describes how he turned about 1,700 priority incidents from two years into categorised step-by-step "Incident Models" (runbooks), stored as plain text in a separate JIRA project. He explains a triage process (rota'd weekly, kept minimal, overseen by experienced staff) and a post-incident review process that feeds a backlog of technical and process debt. It also covers how documentation was maintained by non-SRE engineers and how the work reduced escalation stress, eased onboarding, and enabled further automation.
notable: Turned about 1,700 incidents from two years into categorised runbooks, taking seven months of full-time work
Kept documentation in plain text inside the ticketing system rather than a wiki, to avoid search and update friction
Documentation structure reduced to three parts: problem statement, numbered steps, deeper discussion
caveats: Anecdotal account from one team; the author notes the work took months before paying off
Mentions of the author's paid books (Learn Bash the Hard Way, Learn Git the Hard Way, Docker in Practice) appear on the page as promotion
